what: Houlihan Lokey is an investment bank focused on mid-sized deals, restructuring advice for companies in distress, and valuing illiquid assets for accounting and tax purposes.
customers: Mid-sized companies and private equity owners, creditors in bankruptcies, and firms needing independent valuations.
money: merger and capital raising advice for mid-sized companies
advice to distressed companies and their creditors
moat: Restructuring earns most when mergers earn least, so the two halves offset each other: it is one of the few investment banks that makes money through a downturn.
risks: Advisory revenue is cyclical even with the restructuring hedge
23 times earnings, a premium to other advisory banks
The business is its bankers, who can leave
opportunities: A 16.3% net margin and $402M of free cash flow, with $1.2B of cash against $492M of debt
Revenue recovered from $1.8B to $2.6B in three years
Analysts see about 20% upside, and private equity firms have a record backlog of companies they must eventually sell
watch: Corporate finance fee revenue and the restructuring pipeline.
